```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(zugrpc)
```

gRPC is how many services talk to each other, Spark Connect among them.
It runs only over HTTP/2 and carries its status in HTTP trailers, which
the usual R HTTP clients do not expose. zugrpc speaks the gRPC wire
protocol on top of zuhttp's HTTP/2. You bring the request message,
encoded with zuproto, and get back the response message, its metadata and
its status. Calls can be unary or server-streaming.

```{r fake-server, include = FALSE}
# A fake gRPC server, so that this article runs anywhere: zuhttp's mock
# transport answers each request as a server would, framing included.
frame <- function(text) {
  bytes <- charToRaw(text)
  n <- length(bytes)
  c(as.raw(c(0, n %/% 2^24, n %/% 2^16 %% 256, n %/% 256 %% 256, n %% 256)), bytes)
}
answer <- function(req) {
  ok <- function(body) {
    zuhttp::zu_response(
      200L,
      headers = c("content-type" = "application/grpc+proto", "x-served-by" = "fake"),
      body = body,
      trailers = c("grpc-status" = "0")
    )
  }
  switch(
    sub(".*/", "", req$url),
    SayHello = ok(frame(paste0("hello, ", rawToChar(req$body[-(1:5)])))),
    Count = ok(do.call(c, lapply(c("one", "two", "three"), frame))),
    zuhttp::zu_response(
      200L,
      headers = c(
        "content-type" = "application/grpc+proto",
        "grpc-status" = "5",
        "grpc-message" = "no%20such%20greeting"
      )
    )
  )
}
fake <- zuhttp::zu_client(transport = zuhttp::zu_mock_transport(answer))
```

This article talks to a fake server, built in a hidden chunk with zuhttp's
mock transport, so that it runs anywhere. Its messages are plain text
rather than protobuf, to keep the output readable. Against a real server,
leave out `client = fake`.

## Open a channel

A channel holds what every call to one server shares. An `http://` URL is
cleartext HTTP/2, for a local server. An `https://` URL negotiates HTTP/2
over TLS, with trust settings from `zuhttp::zu_tls()`.

```{r}
ch <- grpc_channel("http://localhost:50051", client = fake)
ch
```

`headers` go on every call, `keepalive` keeps an idle connection checked,
and `max_message` limits the size of a response message.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
grpc_channel(
  "https://spark.example.org:443",
  headers = c(authorization = "Bearer ..."),
  keepalive = grpc_keepalive(time = 60, timeout = 20),
  max_message = 128 * 1024^2
)
```

## Make a unary call

A unary call sends one request message and returns one response message.
The request is a raw vector, usually from `zuproto::proto_encode()`. The
deadline is in seconds, or an absolute `POSIXct`.

```{r}
res <- grpc_call(
  ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayHello",
  request = charToRaw("world"),
  metadata = c("x-request-id" = "42"),
  deadline = 30
)
rawToChar(res$message)
res$headers
res$status
```

## Stream the responses

A server-streaming call returns a stream. Each `$next_message()` returns
one response message, and `NULL` at the end. The server only sends as far
ahead as you read.

```{r}
st <- grpc_stream(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Count", request = raw(), deadline = 600)
while (!is.null(m <- st$next_message())) {
  print(rawToChar(m))
}
st$status()
```

Cancel a stream you no longer need. The connection stays open for other
calls, and a second cancel does nothing.

```{r}
st <- grpc_stream(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Count", request = raw())
rawToChar(st$next_message())
st$cancel()
```

## Handle errors

A call that ends with a status other than `OK` raises a
`zugrpc_error_status` condition. Its class also carries the status, so
you can catch one code.

```{r}
tryCatch(
  grpc_call(ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayGoodbye", request = raw()),
  zugrpc_error_not_found = function(cnd) {
    cnd$grpc_message
  }
)
```

The condition's `details` field holds the decoded `google.rpc.Status`,
with error details such as `ErrorInfo` unpacked. Spark Connect puts its
error class and SQL state there:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tryCatch(
  grpc_stream(spark, "/spark.connect.SparkConnectService/ExecutePlan",
              request = bad_plan)$next_message(),
  zugrpc_error_status = function(cnd) {
    cnd$details$details$ErrorInfo$metadata[["errorClass"]]
  }
)
```

`grpc_status_codes()` lists the codes a call can end with.

```{r}
grpc_status_codes()
```

## Close and inspect

Closing a channel cancels its open streams.

```{r}
grpc_close(ch)
```

`zugrpc_info()` reports the zuhttp version, whether it speaks HTTP/2 and
its TLS backend.

```{r}
zugrpc_info()
```
